parts.label: (a)
parts.text: State what is meant by work done.

markscheme_points.text: force × displacement in the direction of the force

hints: Hint 1: Think about what happens energetically when you push something and it moves - which part of the movement actually counts for work?
parts.proper_answer: Work done is the product of force and displacement in the direction of the force.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **What work really means**
You do work whenever a force causes energy to be transferred by moving something. If you push hard on a wall that does not move, no energy is transferred, so no work is done.

Step 2: **The precise definition**
Only the displacement along the line of the force counts. So in words: $$W = F \times s$$ where $s$ is the displacement in the direction of $F$. That is $\text{force} \times \text{displacement in the direction of the force}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Use the answer to (a) to determine the SI base units of power.

markscheme_points.text: P = Fs / t = (kg m s⁻² × m) / s

hints: Hint 1: Start from how power is linked to work and time, then replace work with your idea from (a). What are the units of each part?
Hint 2: Break force down into its base units from $F = ma$, then combine with the extra metre from work and divide by time.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Link power to work**
Power is the rate of doing work: $$P = \frac{W}{t} = \frac{Fs}{t}$$ So the unit of power is: $$\text{unit of }P = \frac{\text{unit of }F \times \text{unit of }s}{\text{unit of }t}$$

Step 2: **Break force into base units**
From $F = ma$, force has units $\text{kg} \times \text{m s}^{-2} = \text{kg m s}^{-2}$. Displacement $s$ is in $\text{m}$ and time $t$ is in $\text{s}$.

Step 3: **Combine to get base units**
$$\text{unit of }P = \frac{(\text{kg m s}^{-2}) \times \text{m}}{\text{s}} = \text{kg m}^{2}\text{ s}^{-3}$$ These are all SI base units: $\text{kg}$, $\text{m}$, $\text{s}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.part_stem:
The maximum useful output power $P$ of a car travelling on a horizontal road is given by $$P = v^3b$$ where $v$ is the maximum speed of the car and $b$ is a constant.

For the car,

$P = 84\ \text{kW} \pm 5\%$
and $b = 0.56 \pm 7\%$ in SI units.

parts.label: (c)(i)
hints: Hint 1: Look at the relation $P = v^3 b$ and think how you would isolate $v$ on its own before putting any numbers in.
Hint 2: Check the prefix on the power value - what must $84\text{ kW}$ become in standard watts for SI consistency?
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Rearrange for the speed**
You are given $P = v^3 b$. To get $v$ alone, divide by $b$ and then take the cube root: $$v^3 = \frac{P}{b}$$ $$v = \left(\frac{P}{b}\right)^{1/3}$$

Step 2: **Substitute with correct units**
Convert power to watts: $P = 84\text{ kW} = 84 \times 10^3\text{ W}$. Then: $$v^3 = \frac{84 \times 10^3}{0.56} = 1.5 \times 10^5$$ $$v = (1.5 \times 10^5)^{1/3} \approx 53\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Hint 2: Check the prefix on the power value - what must $84\text{ kW}$ become in standard watts for SI consistency?

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Determine the absolute uncertainty in the value of $v$.
hints: Hint 1: From $v^3 = P/b$, think how the percentage uncertainties in $P$ and $b$ combine to give the percentage uncertainty in $v^3$.
Hint 2: Remember the rule for a power: if you take a cube root, what happens to the percentage uncertainty? Then how do you turn that into an absolute value?
parts.proper_answer: Percentage uncertainty in $v = 4\%$, absolute uncertainty $= 0.04 \times 53 \approx \pm 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Find percentage uncertainty in $v^3$**
Since $v^3 = P/b$, for a multiply/divide calculation you add the percentage uncertainties: $$\Delta(v^3)\% = 5\% + 7\% = 12\%$$

Step 2: **Deal with the cube power**
When a quantity is raised to power $n$, its percentage uncertainty is multiplied by $n$. Here $v = (v^3)^{1/3}$, so you divide by 3: $$\Delta v\% = \frac{12\%}{3} = 4\%$$

Step 3: **Convert to absolute uncertainty**
Absolute uncertainty = fractional uncertainty $\times$ value: $$\Delta v = 0.04 \times 53 \approx 2.1\text{ m s}^{-1} \approx \pm 2\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
